source.authorityName: Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE)
source.extractionTool: pdftotext (poppler) and pdfplumber text layer; notation checked against page renders (pypdfium2)
source.usage: Official CISCE publication, freely available on cisce.org; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.
source.notes: Every page footer prints 'ISC (CLASS XII) SPECIMEN QUESTION PAPER 2026' (pages 1-14) or 'ISC (CLASS XII) SPECIMEN ANSWER KEY 2026' (pages 15-24); examYear 2026 is the examination year the specimen is published for. Listed on cisce.org under specimen-question-papers-isc-class-xii-2026. The key is headed 'ANSWER KEY (Equivalent answers are acceptable.)'. 'page' is the physical PDF page of the question. Paper prints 'Maximum Marks: 70', three hours, 20 questions in Sections A (14 marks: Question 1 with parts (A)(i)-(vii) MCQ and (B)(i)-(vii) short answers, 1 mark each), B (Q2-Q8, 2 marks each), C (Q9-Q17, 3 marks each) and D (Q18-Q20, 5 marks each). Internal choices (OR) in Q2, Q4, Q10, Q12, Q18, Q19; alternatives are labelled (i)/(ii) as printed and share choiceGroup = question number. Sub-parts inside a question carry no separate printed marks, so each question (or OR alternative) is one entry with its sub-parts in the text; Q20 (i) and (ii) are both compulsory and are kept as one 5-mark entry for the same reason. Cognitive tags (Recall, Understanding, Application, Analysis) are printed in green and are reproduced as printed; where the parts of a combined entry carry different tags the field is omitted. The text layer loses many symbols (λ, α, ε₀, μ₀, ∝, subscripts and powers of ten); these were rebuilt from the rendered pages and flagged per question. Figures, circuit diagrams and graphs are not reproduced; answers that exist only as images (Q1(B)(i) graph, Q1(A)(iii) graph option, Q10(i) final expression, Q16(ii) ray diagram) are flagged and not rebuilt. The 'Useful constants and relations' table on page 14 is not included as a question.

questions.text:
The current (I)-voltage (V) graphs for a conductor are given at two different temperatures T₁ and T₂.
(a) At which temperature T₁ or T₂ is the resistance higher?
(b) Which temperature T₁ or T₂ is higher?

officialAnswer.text:
(a) For the I-V graph, the slope of the I-V graph gives the conductance R = V/I = 1/tanθ. Since θ₁ > θ₂, tanθ₁ > tanθ₂. So Resistance at T₁ < Resistance at T₂.

officialAnswer.text: The total emf in the circuit is, E+E = 2E. The total resistance in the circuit is, R+r₁+r₂. The current in the circuit is given by: I = 2E/(R+r₁+r₂). Given V = E - Ir₁ = 0 ∴ Ir₁ = E ∴ 2E/(R + r₁ + r₂) × r₁ = E. R = r₁ − r₂

officialAnswer.text: F = (1/4πε₀) · (Q×1)/x² = (1/4πε₀) Q/x². dW = -Fdx = -(1/4πε₀)(Q/x²) dx. V = W = ∫_∞^r dW = ∫_∞^r −(1/4πε₀)(Q/x²) dx. V = (1/4πε₀) Q/r. This is the desired expression.

(b) In Rutherford’s scattering experiment when an alpha particle (charge = +2e, mass = 4mₚ) approaches a gold nucleus (Z = 79), it is continuously repelled, so it loses its kinetic energy(K) and its potential energy increases. Finally, α-particle comes to rest momentarily when whole of the kinetic energy is change into the potential energy of the charge at that distance from the nucleus. Let this distance be r₀ after which α-particle returns back again due to electrostatic repulsion.
Using the above information, derive an expression for r₀.

(a) (1) Region C (2) Region A (3) Region B
(b) At the distance of closest approach r₀ this energy has changed into potential energy U of the α-particle. U = (1/4πϵ₀) × (Ze·2e)/r₀, where Z = 79 is the atomic number of gold nucleus. Thus we have, K = (1/4πϵ₀) × 2(79)e²/r₀; r₀ = (1/4πϵ₀) × 158e²/K

(i) A band gap is the distance between the valence band of electrons and the conduction band. Essentially, the band gap represents the minimum energy that is required to excite an electron up to a state in the conduction band where it can participate in conduction. The lower energy level is the valence band, and thus if a gap exists between this level and the higher energy conduction band, energy must be input for electrons to become free.
